NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
Identity has to land while decisions.md is still one file. The later split moves F/D bodies; fragments that today collide inside one file become cross-file references whose target is undefined for the whole interval between bundles. Delimiter-preserving slugs make F9.1 and F91 distinct so the engine rewrite is mechanical over a set whose every member has exactly one target.
This is not preservation of working GitHub links. GitHub heading slugs strip punctuation, so 0 of the current f/d fragments match a generated heading id. Explicit <a id name> anchors are new targets. The first-token strip-dot convention is what authors already typed; keep-dot is what those destinations must become.
Same-token duplicates (F19, F21, F21 correction, F27.1, F27.1 amendment) are not strip-dot collisions. Keep-dot alone does not separate them. The qualifier-suffix rule is the smallest addition that makes every heading unique without renaming canonical Token — titles and without treating f21-correction as a one-off.

Alternatives.Alternative: Strip-dot slugs (F9.1 → f91, F108.1 → f1081). Pros: matches every current destination except #f21-correction; no mechanical rewrite of unique dotted citations. Cons: 29 collision groups at measurement, including F9.1 / F91; the later split inherits every collision; f21-correction stays a hand-assigned exception. Rejected. This is the earlier proposal the brief retired.

Keep-dot only, no qualifier suffix (F9.1 → f9.1; F21 correction also → f21). Pros: one rule; eliminates the 26 distinct-token strip-dot groups. Cons: three remaining collisions (F19, F21, F27.1); #f21-correction would not match its heading. Rejected. The brief's claim that keep-dot eliminates every collision group is false until the qualifier-suffix clause is added.

GitHub full-heading slugs as ids, fragments rewritten to match. Pros: auto-generated heading ids would then match if GitHub's algorithm is reimplemented exactly. Cons: 0 of 182 current fragments match those slugs already; ids become long title strings that churn when a heading is edited; the later index wants short stable tokens. Rejected.

Keep-dot plus qualifier suffix on same-token duplicates only. Pros: distinct tokens never collide; the three remaining pairs become f19 / f19s, f21 / f21-correction, f27.1 / f27.1-amendment; unique correction headings stay f74.1 so mechanical restore still works; f21-correction is the ordinary suffix, not an exception. Cons: the possessive F19's rule is a third shape, closed here. Chosen.

Always suffix correction / amendment even when unique (F74.1 correction → f74.1-correction). Pros: uniform heading-shape to slug. Cons: mechanical restore of #f741 would miss the new id; every unique correction heading becomes a reading case. Rejected.

Record the 79 colliding citations as a table in the spec or a new inventory file. Pros: a reviewer can read intent without the diff. Cons: Constraints must not pin counts of a file this bundle changes; the table rots the moment a later sentence is appended; the corrected fragment is already the durable record; the validator proves uniqueness, not intent. Rejected. The git diff of those destinations is the reading record.

Put the uniqueness check in ngrace lint. Pros: one diagnostic surface. Cons: docs markdown is outside the lint artifact universe (src/grace-lint.test.ts:1879); adding .md to CODE_EXTENSIONS overturns that test; this file is not an XML artifact. Rejected. scripts/ plus validate:ci is the precedent (validate-determinism.ts).

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Three-genre split, retirement triggers, ceilings, registry.xml, and codifiedIn / taughtIn checks. Owner: C-RECORD-RETIREMENT. This bundle only makes that rewrite mechanical.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mechanical. [F88.2](#f882) today. Only heading F88.2 strip-dots to f882. After apply the destination is #f88.2 and the heading carries id="f88.2".
Reading. [F93](#f93) today. Headings F9.3 and F93 both strip-dot to f93. The citing sentence decides. After apply the destination is #f9.3 or #f93, never left as a token that silently binds to F93.
Qualifier. [F21 correction](#f21-correction) today already names the suffix this grammar produces. The canonical F21 heading gets id="f21". Both stay.
